intro.author: Traditionally Solomon. The heading 'which is Solomon's' (1:1) can mean by, for, or about Solomon, so authorship is debated.
intro.written: Traditionally during Solomon's reign (about 970–930 BC); many scholars date its final form later because of features of its Hebrew.
intro.audience: Israel; within the poems the bride often speaks to 'the daughters of Jerusalem,' who act like a chorus
intro.setting: A collection of love poems in which a woman and a man take turns speaking. In Hebrew the pronouns show who is speaking, so many modern Bibles add headings. Scenes move between vineyards, flocks and gardens and the streets and court of Jerusalem. Jewish and Christian readers have long also read it as a picture of God's love for His people, and Jewish communities traditionally read it at Passover.
intro.purpose: To celebrate the love between a man and a woman as a good and powerful gift; many in both Jewish and Christian tradition also see in it the love between God and His people.
intro.bigIdea: Love is strong as death and worth more than all wealth, and it must be awakened in its proper time.
